title: John McWhorter: The Trickster Trips Up?
author: Ishmael Reed
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/mcwhortermaher-680x501.png)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/07/31/john-
mcwhorter-the-trickster-trips-up/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/mcwhortermaher-680x501.png)

John McWhorter on Bill Maher talking about alleged "black fragility." (Screen
capture from video posted to YouTube.)

_John McWhorter is so valuable to the enemies of Blacks that he has survived
wishing the president were_ __assassinated.___Or has_ _he?_

I first heard of John McWhorter when the _Daily Californian,_ a newspaper
distributed on the campus of the University of California at Berkeley, asked
me for a comment on his book, _Losing the Race: Self Sabotage in Black
America_. I said I read it twice in five minutes, because the book rehashes
some of the arguments made by Shelby Steele in his book, _The Content of Our
Character_. Steele is a better writer.

Despite the thousands of reports and studies that say otherwise, both claim
that the problems facing Blacks result from their personal behavior or that
racism is not as big a deal as a century or so of Black writers have claimed.

If I were ever inclined to succumb to such thinking, living in the Black
Oakland inner city since 1979 set me straight. Though the neighborhood had
been neglected by the city government, abandoned by absentee landlords and the
police, red-lined, and beset by crack houses, which resulted in occasional
gunfire, most of the kids on my block left the neighborhood for the middle
class. Only when the neighborhood became gentrified in 2013 did conditions
improve.

After he read my comments, McWhorter called my home and angrily promised to
“wipe up the floor” with me in a debate. I arranged a debate on a popular Hip
Hop show, “Hard Knock Radio,” moderated by Davey D. McWhorter backed out.

Because of his blame-the-victim book, McWhorter was invited to New York by the
Manhattan Institute, which promises its fellows that their association with
the Institute will lead to publicity. The Manhattan Institute was the
originator of “[Stop and
Frisk,](https://www.nytimes.com/2012/08/07/nyregion/for-women-in-street-stops-
deeper-humiliation.html)” which was declared unconstitutional after thousands
of young Black and Hispanic men were stopped without cause. Black and brown
women complained that the police used the measure as an excuse to molest them.
[1] The Institute’s “broken windows” theory that physical or social disorder
directly causes individuals to commit more serious crimes has been
[debunked](https://cssh.northeastern.edu/sccj/2019/05/21/researchers-debunk-
broken-windows-theory-after-35-years/). [2]

The Manhattan Institute is a recipient of funds from the usual right-wing
sources, such as the Lynde and Harry Bradley Foundation. The two brothers
supported the John Birch Society and helped to finance Charles Murray’s
Eugenics book, _The Bell Curve_. Charles Murray’s ethnic group is Scots-Irish,
whom Benjamin Franklin called “Christian white savages.”

When I finally debated McWhorter on Michael Eric Dyson’s show, I found him
ignorant of the Manhattan Institute’s history. McWhorter didn’t know that it
was founded by William Casey, Ronald Reagan’s CIA chief, who might have been
indicted for Iran-Contra had he not died.

I’m also sure that when he defends Charles Murray, author of _The Bell Curve,_
which argues that white people are smarter than the rest of us, McWhorter was
probably not aware that the other outfit that picked up the bill for Murray’s
book was the [Pioneer Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_Fund), a
“race betterment” outfit which has Nazi ties.

> Started in 1937 by textile magnate Wickliffe Draper, the Pioneer Fund’s
> original mandate was to pursue ‘race betterment’ by promoting the genetic
> stock of those ‘deemed to be descended predominantly from white persons who
> settled in the original thirteen states prior to the adoption of the
> Constitution.’ Today, it still funds studies of race and intelligence, as
> well as eugenics, the ‘science’ of breeding superior human beings that was
> discredited by various Nazi atrocities. [3]

Odd that Andrew Sullivan endorsed _The Bell Curve_ in _The New Republic_. In
Nazi Germany, Sullivan, a gay man, would have been placed in a concentration
camp like Clifford, the gay character in John A. Williams’ novel, _Clifford’s
Blues._

At one point in the Dyson program, McWhorter insisted that I be civil to him.
I said I didn’t feel it necessary to be civil to a Nazi sympathizer. McWhorter
has proposed that a serum might be necessary to make Blacks less violent and
to bridge the I.Q. gap. [4] This is a dangerous idea since Blacks are still
experimented upon without their knowledge. That includes the leprosy
experiments on prisoners at Attica in the 1970s, funded by the U.S. Public
Health Service. The University of Pennsylvania apologized for experiments on
Black prisoners at Holmesburg Prison.

McWhorter became a professor at Columbia University and was hired at the _New
York Times,_ where _The Bell Curve_ received a positive review, and where
other writers embrace Eugenics, but none has suggested that Blacks should
undergo gene editing. McWhorter has flirted with the idea. [5]

But at the _NYT_ it’s convenient to put a Black face on the Eugenics theory.
John’s. His job at The Times seems to be challenging the ideas of Black public
intellectuals who claim that racism is still pervasive in American life, a job
that doesn’t require much intellectual heft, or, as I have put it, every time
we say tomato, he says tomahto.

A political shape shifter, he now calls himself a Democrat, but not many
Democrats are into Eugenics.

Of course, when an outfit like the _NYT_ hires a token, they receive immunity
from rebuttal. The Times poses as a bastion of free speech, yet there is no
Black columnist who is as left as McWhorter is right. Black columnist Jamelle
Boule is a moderate.

McWhorter never forgot my comment about his book, and so I became an early
target of his wrath when he wrote a self-pitying piece in _Commentary_ ,_Feb.
2004,_ auditioning for the position of Black right-wing intellectual for hire.
Journalist Jack White, the late Manning Marble, and I were the article’s
villains. He also derided Congresswoman Maxine Waters.

For example, he doubted my experience with racial profiling. He said it never
happened to him:

> Not once to date have I had a nasty, intrusive run-in with the police,
> despite being no stranger to nightlife in cities like New York,
> Philadelphia, and Oakland, and despite having driven a beat-up car in tony
> white neighborhoods on a regular basis when, as a graduate student, I earned
> extra money playing piano at parties. [6]

His denial of my experience must have drawn the attention of the Manhattan
Neo-Con clique, former working-class radicals who turned right and
publications like the _New York Times_ and _The Atlantic Monthly._

Reviewing _Losing The Race_ in _Commentary_ , a writer said that Blacks were
“paranoid” when they make claims of racism. Something that Holocaust deniers
have told Jews for fifty years.

Twenty years later, McWhorter is still using a hackneyed formula. When Blacks
complain about racist treatment, McWhorter still dismisses such claims as
delusional. He doesn’t have to present facts. His dismissals are often
flippant.

He disputed those who condemned Daniel Penny’s acquittal for the murder of
Jordan Neely, a homeless Black man, as a racist act. I wish those describing
Penny or his acquittal as racist might consider things from another vantage
point.” [7]

On July 16th, he was still at it, this time defending the SAT Test in his Op-
ed entitled **" **A Test Isn’t Racist,” [8] contradicting a study published by
the National Education Association that concluded otherwise. [9]

The editor of _Commentary,_ where McWhorter’s audition piece appeared,was
Norman Podhoretz, who, with his wife Midge, a homophobe, posed as advocates of
the nuclear family. They earned money by criticizing the morals of non-wed
Black teenage mothers when Podhoretz’s own morality was questioned by Theodor
Soloratoff writing in _The Nation_

> In the past year or two he had teamed up with Norman Mailer, the lead rebel,
> iconoclast and sensualist of the New York scene. The result was a hard-
> drinking, sexually liberated Norman who didn’t seem to spend many evenings
> at home. Our editorial meetings were often punctuated by phone calls from
> Mailer, who appeared to have open access to Norman. We always knew it was
> “the other Norman”–as Sherry referred to him, with her droll roll of the
> eyes–because the butch side of Norman would emerge as he responded to
> Mailer’s latest brainstorm or piece of gossip or plan for the night’s
> revels.10

Because I’m on to McWhorter’s hustle, I’ve been ridiculed in _City Journal_ ,
the Institute’s publication. I was called an “old timer” for challenging the
premise of the musical “Hamilton” that Alexander Hamilton, a slave owner, was
“an ardent abolitionist.” The Times backed up my claim. [11] My reply was that
if the Institute hadn’t taken tobacco money, maybe some of their subscribers
would have lived as long as I have.

Hard on poor men who do squeegee services, the Institute hasn’t noticed that
the CEOs of the tobacco companies that support the Institute lied about the
effect of smoking cigarettes on lung diseases. Maybe McWhorter can write a
tough love piece about them for the Times. But that would be beyond his
assignment. His job is to scold homeless Black men who walk in the aisles of
New York subways.

The Manhattan literati have been imposing tokens on Black writers for over one
hundred years, but they usually mess up, as with Claude McKay, who challenged
his sponsors’ emphasis on class rather than race. He found more sympathy for
his condition from the Catholic Church than from socialists like Mike Gold.
The Manhattan literari exiled James Baldwin, when he insulted Actors Studio’s
Lee Strasberg in his novel _Tell Me How Long the Train’s Been Gone._ After
that, according to Truman Capote, Baldwin was treated like “shit.”

I was instrumental in getting Baldwin two university appointments, yet he lied
and said I called him a “cocksucker,” every time I encountered him. He
betrayed me like he betrayed his other benefactor, Richard Wright. Chester
Himes, one of those whom Baldwin had to step on in order to reach the top,
said that Baldwin was ambitious.

Another token, Stanley Crouch, was admired by his Neo-Con sponsors when he
bullied Black writers, but when he slapped Dale Peck, a white man, Crouch was
exiled from Manhattan to Brooklyn, where he came to a pitiful end.

In 2024, McWhorter said that he wished someone would assassinate Donald Trump!
Even though Trump, like McWhorter, endorses Eugenics!12 Lordy!

Columbia University, where he works, capitulated to Donald Trump. Trump now
owns Columbia. They’ll probably give him an honorary degree like Harvard gave
to mass murderer Andrew Jackson, a former president who most resembles Trump.
An honor that outraged John Adams. Donald Trump owns McWhorter’s job.

McWhorter never apologized to Black Americans for the often nasty, sarcastic
stream of insults aimed at the community at the behest of his sponsors, but he
just about groveled on his hands and knees apologizing for his statement
wishing that Trump were dead. Can you imagine the fate of a Black public
intellectual of the left making a threat against the president? Wouldn’t he or
she be visited by the Secret Service?

Yet McWhorter survives because he says what the enemies of Blacks say in
private. For now.

**Notes.**

1 <https://www.nytimes.com/2012/08/07/nyregion/for-women-in-street-stops-
deeper-humiliation.html>

2 Criminologists and sociologists have largely debunked the Broken Windows
Theory, finding little empirical evidence that physical or social disorder
directly causes individuals to commit more serious crimes. Extensive research,
including major meta-analyses like the [Northeastern University School of
Criminology and Criminal
Justice](https://cssh.northeastern.edu/sccj/2019/05/21/researchers-debunk-
broken-windows-theory-after-35-years/) study, has demonstrated that
neighborhood disorder does not inherently escalate crime. The theory's
premise—that minor offenses act as a gateway to major crimes—does not hold up
to scrutiny.

3 <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_Fund>

4\. Ann Brown, [John McWhorter: Racial Equality May Mean Genetic Editing to
Close Racial IQ Gap](https://moguldom.com/335699/john-mcwhorter-racial-
equality-may-mean-genetic-editing-to-close-racial-iq-gap/#google_vignette),
_Muguldom Nation_ , Feb 09, 2021.

5 <https://fair.org/home/at-elite-media-scientific-racists-fit-in-fine/>

6 John H. McWhorter. “[Still Losing the
Race?](https://www.commentary.org/author/john-mcwhorter-2/)” A personal
inquiry into why pessimism and victimology remain the key tenets of "advanced"
black thought. February 2002, _Commentary_ magazine.

7 McWhorter, John. "[A Killing on the F
Train](https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/09/opinion/jordan-neely-subway-
death.html)," _New York Times,_ May 9, 2023.

8 McWhorter, John. "[A Test Isn’t
Racist.](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/16/opinion/new-york-high-school-test-
